basic_info.name: g-AMIE (guardrailed-AMIE)
basic_info.description: g-AMIE is a Google DeepMind/Google Research multi-agent conversational diagnostic AI that performs patient history taking under a hard guardrail: it is explicitly forbidden from communicating any 'individualized medical advice' (any tailored diagnosis or management plan). It is the oversight-oriented extension of AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), built on Gemini 2.0 Flash. The load-bearing fact is its asynchronous-oversight paradigm: after intake, g-AMIE writes a SOAP note plus a draft patient message and proposed differential/management plan, which an overseeing primary-care physician (o-PCP) reviews, edits and authorizes in a purpose-built 'clinician cockpit'; because oversight is decoupled from the real-time conversation, it can happen asynchronously. In a randomized, blinded virtual OSCE study across 60 scenarios with professional patient actors, g-AMIE outperformed two control groups (early-career PCPs and NP/PAs operating under identical guardrails) on intake quality, case summarization, and proposed differential/management quality, while no g-AMIE consultation was rated as definitely containing individualized medical advice (versus 15% of g-PCP and 5% of g-NP/PA scenarios). PCP oversight of g-AMIE took roughly 60% of the time of a full text-based consultation. It is a text-only, English, cloud-hosted research prototype; no FHIR/ABDM emission and no offline mode.
basic_info.organization: Google DeepMind and Google Research (with co-authors from Harvard Medical School / Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center); study run with GoodLabs Studio and CEP America/Vituity
basic_info.country: United States and United Kingdom (Google DeepMind, London / Google Research, US)

technical_features.what_it_does: Conducts patient-facing text history taking, then produces a clinician-facing case summary and a proposed differential diagnosis and management plan for human authorization. For Module C the relevant capability is its structured, physician-ready case summary (SOAP note) plus its guardrail architecture: the system separates information gathering from advice giving, generates a SOAP note and draft patient message with constrained decoding, and hands both to a physician for review, edit and sign-off. A dedicated guardrail agent screens every outgoing patient turn and rewrites it if individualized medical advice is detected, ensuring the summary/plan is never surfaced to the patient before physician authorization. It does not emit a standards-conformant clinical document (no FHIR Composition/Bundle, no NRCeS profile) - the artifact is a free-text SOAP note plus a patient message.
technical_features.architecture: Multi-agent system built on Gemini 2.0 Flash. Three specialised agents: (1) a clinical dialogue agent that runs a three-phase intake protocol (Phase 1 broad history intake with chain-of-thought summarisation; Phase 2 differential-diagnosis validation via targeted questions; Phase 3 conclusion - summarise/confirm with the patient, invite questions, set expectations that the transcript goes to an overseeing physician); (2) a guardrail agent that screens every dialogue-agent response for individualized medical advice before it reaches the patient and rewrites non-compliant responses, capped at a maximum of three revision attempts per turn to meet latency constraints; (3) a SOAP-note generation agent that sequentially generates Subjective and Objective sections (summarisation) first, then Assessment and Plan (inferential reasoning), then a patient-facing message, using constrained decoding to enforce section structure. A 'clinician cockpit' web UI - co-designed in a participatory study with 10 outpatient PCPs - presents the chief complaint, the full transcript (for grounding/verification), the four editable SOAP sections, and patient-message options, with o-PCP actions to sign off or request follow-up. Auto-raters also powered by Gemini 2.0 Flash are used for scalable evaluation against scenario ground truth.
technical_features.inputs: Real-time text dialogue with the patient (chief complaint, history of present illness, review of systems, past medical/family/social history, medications, allergies). No vitals, no uploaded documents, no structured FHIR input, no imaging in this study. Evaluation additionally consumes OSCE scenario packs with ground-truth conditions, red-flag question checklists and recommended next steps.
technical_features.outputs: A SOAP note (Subjective, Objective, Assessment with differential diagnosis and justification, Plan) plus a draft patient message describing proposed diagnosis and next steps; a ranked differential diagnosis and management plan; the raw consultation transcript; and an auto-rater quality scorecard. Formats are free text / structured JSON within the system, not an HL7 FHIR Composition or NRCeS OPConsultRecord Bundle - there is no documented standards-coded emission, no SNOMED CT/LOINC/ICD coding of the output, and no document Bundle assembly.
technical_features.standards_compliance: [uncertain] No FHIR, HL7, NRCeS/ABDM or terminology-standard conformance is claimed or demonstrated. The system does use the SOAP note structure (Weed's problem-oriented medical record format) and evaluates note quality with adapted QNote and PDQI-9-style rubrics, and communication/intake with validated clinical-education instruments (PACES, PCCBP, GMCPQ). Individualized medical advice detection was validated against a purpose-built annotated benchmark: three medical students labelled 100 AMIE dialogues (1,309 turns) in triplicate, giving 80% inter-rater agreement; Gemini 2.0 Flash with few-shot prompting reached 95.96% accuracy on the held-out classification task. Coding of diagnoses or medications to SNOMED CT / ICD / LOINC is not part of the work. Standards conformance is therefore not validated and not claimed.
technical_features.offline_capability: None. g-AMIE runs on Gemini 2.0 Flash served through Google Cloud APIs, and the paper's code-availability statement explicitly points to Gemini being available via Google Cloud APIs; the multi-agent techniques are described in text only and no code or offline weights are released. There is no on-device, edge, store-and-forward or local encrypted storage mechanism described, and connectivity is assumed for every consultation and every oversight interaction.
technical_features.languages_supported: English only. All OSCE scenarios, patient actors and clinician participants were US/Canada based and the study was text-only in English; no Hindi, Devanagari, Hinglish or other Indic-language capability is reported or implied.
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud research prototype. Inference runs on Google Cloud (Gemini 2.0 Flash); the clinician cockpit is a web interface (purpose-built for the study, not a shipped product). No on-premises, kiosk or room-server deployment is described, and no local hardware requirements are stated because computation is entirely server-side. Successor AMIE work has moved to real-world clinic feasibility studies and a nationwide virtual-care trial, but always as cloud-hosted research infrastructure, not an installable on-site system.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Randomized blinded virtual OSCE, 60 scenarios, judged by independent physicians plus Gemini-based auto-raters. Diagnostic accuracy (auto-rated against scenario ground truth): 81.7% top-1 for g-AMIE vs 53.3% for guardrailed early-career PCPs (g-PCP) and 63.3% for guardrailed NP/PAs (g-NP/PA); 91.7% when the full differential is considered. Management-plan ground-truth coverage: 38.5% g-AMIE vs 32.9% g-PCP and 34.1% g-NP/PA. Guardrail adherence (human-rated): 90.0% for g-AMIE and 91.7% for g-NP/PA vs 71.7% for g-PCP; zero g-AMIE consultations were rated 'definitely contains medical advice' vs 15% of g-PCP and 5% of g-NP/PA scenarios, and where advice leaked it was a single turn (up to four for g-PCP). Red-flag symptom coverage: 64.2% g-AMIE vs 40.0% g-PCP, 51.7% g-NP/PA. Draft patient message accepted by o-PCP in 93.3% of g-AMIE and g-NP/PA scenarios vs 80% for g-PCP. Composite overseen consultation rated poor or worse in only 20% of g-AMIE scenarios vs 35% g-PCP / 25% g-NP/PA. Guardrail classifier itself scored 95.96% accuracy against the human-labelled medical-advice benchmark. SOAP notes were rated by physicians as more complete, accurate and readable than controls, but also significantly more verbose.
performance_metrics.latency: No per-turn or end-to-end generation latency figures are reported. The only timing result is oversight time: o-PCP oversight of g-AMIE took around 60% of the time required for a full text-based simulated consultation (equivalently, roughly 40% shorter than the non-overseen PCP text consultations measured in prior AMIE work). The guardrail agent's revision loop is capped at three attempts per turn specifically to satisfy latency constraints, but the resulting wall-clock latency is not quantified. Successor AMIE (Video) work reports ~2.6 s mean turn latency with asynchronous agent orchestration, but that is a different, later system.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: [uncertain] Not applicable in the conventional sense and not published: g-AMIE is entirely cloud-hosted on Gemini 2.0 Flash and the paper states no local RAM/CPU/VRAM requirement. Internally the workload is multi-agent LLM inference (dialogue agent, guardrail agent, SOAP-note agent, plus Gemini auto-raters), which is far beyond a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk and cannot be self-hosted from the released materials because neither weights nor code are provided.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Study scale only: 60 clinical scenarios (30 expected to be independently diagnosable by PAs and 30 not), with US-recruited clinicians - 20 board-certified PCPs with <=5 years of experience (median 4.5), 10 NPs (median 8 years) and 10 PAs (median 6 years) as control groups, plus supervising PCPs with >=5 years of experience, validated US/Canada patient actors, and independent physician raters. Each patient actor enacted the same scenario across g-AMIE and both control groups. There is no deployment, user, or production-volume metric because the system is a research prototype.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: A randomized, blinded, virtual Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) study with asynchronous oversight, plus Gemini-based auto-raters. Three-step design: (1) patient actors consult g-AMIE, g-PCP or g-NP/PA, producing SOAP notes and patient messages; (2) overseeing PCPs review/edit/authorize in the clinician cockpit and rate the experience; (3) independent physicians post-evaluate transcripts, unedited and edited notes and messages against scenario ground truth. Rubrics adapt prior AMIE/OSCE instruments: PACES, PCCBP, GMCPQ for intake and communication; a modified QNote rubric for SOAP-note readability/completeness/accuracy; plus new oversight-specific rubrics for decision quality, note sufficiency for downstream care, and detection of guardrail violations. Auto-raters (Gemini 2.0 Flash) provide diagnostic top-1/full accuracy and management-plan coverage. The work is an arXiv preprint (July 2025) and, as of verification, not a peer-reviewed journal publication; the authors repeatedly caution that the workflow is AI-centric, unfamiliar to clinicians, text-only, actor-simulated, and not representative of real clinical practice, and that comparisons should not be read as evidence that g-AMIE outperforms clinicians.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: g-AMIE is the strongest research prior art for Module C's physician-attestation and structured-summary design. It validates three things MediKiosk needs: (1) it is feasible for an LLM-driven intake to produce a physician-ready structured case summary whose quality is judged at or above early-career clinicians under blinded comparison; (2) a hard guardrail can keep the patient-facing intake free of individualized advice while still allowing a differential and management plan to be prepared for the physician - directly analogous to MediKiosk's 'elicit-never-diagnose + physician-only Assessment & Plan'; (3) decoupling intake from oversight is time-efficient (oversight ~60% of a full consultation), which is the core economics MediKiosk relies on for 2-5-minute OPD slots. It also supplies a ready-made evaluation harness: the clinician-cockpit concept, the rubric set (PACES/PCCBP/GMCPQ + modified QNote + oversight rubrics), and the guardrail-adherence metric. It does NOT supply an offline, NRCeS/ABDM-conformant, bilingual or patient-kiosk precedent - its output is a free-text English SOAP note on cloud infrastructure.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) the deterministic guardrail-agent pattern - a separate classifier that screens every outgoing patient turn for disallowed advice and rewrites it - as a concrete model for a rule-based 'no-diagnosis' enforcement layer at the kiosk, which is auditable and cheap compared with relying on prompt-following alone; (b) the guardrail's validation methodology (a small human-labelled benchmark of dialogues/turns, measured classifier accuracy) as the way to demonstrate a safety control works; (c) the three-phase intake protocol (broad history -> targeted validation -> summarise-and-confirm-conclusion) as a template for Module A's conversational flow and for Module C's read-back; (d) the 'clinician cockpit' UX primitives - chief complaint at top, full transcript alongside the summary for grounding, one editable block per section, explicit accept/request-follow-up action - as the Module C physician review screen; (e) the oversight-oriented rubric set and the 'oversight time as a fraction of a full consultation' KPI. Reject: (a) letting the AI generate a differential diagnosis and management plan at all - MediKiosk's elicit-never-diagnose constraint is stricter, and g-AMIE's own results show physician edits to an AI differential can reduce quality, so a deterministic renderer that surfaces only elicited facts is safer; (b) cloud-only Gemini dependency and absence of released code/weights (incompatible with offline-first, India data residency and the CPU/iGPU kiosk budget); (c) verbose free-text SOAP notes without codes - Module C must emit coded, profile-validated OPConsultRecord sections; (d) treating the verbosity as a strength, since the paper itself notes edits most often shortened g-AMIE notes.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Cloud-only (Gemini 2.0 Flash via Google Cloud APIs) with no offline, on-prem or local-storage path, and no code or model weights released - the architecture is described in prose only, so it cannot be reproduced or self-hosted. Text-only and English-only; no Indic language support. Simulation-bound evidence: 60 constructed OSCE scenarios with patient actors, not real patients, with authors stating results 'do not replicate existing clinical practices and likely underestimate clinicians' capabilities'; the oversight workflow was explicitly unfamiliar to the human control groups, so cross-group comparisons are confounded. Guardrail compliance was rated by a single evaluator per case despite known rater disagreement (80% agreement in the development labelling), and the notion of 'individualized medical advice' is inherently ambiguous - g-AMIE sometimes shared personalised-but-arguably-permissible information. Asynchronous oversight did not reliably improve composite performance (physician edits more often reduced diagnostic quality for g-AMIE than improved it, and in 43.3% of cases the patient message was not edited appropriately); reviewing verbose AI notes imposes real cognitive load. No standards conformance, no coding, and no ABDM/India-residency story. All authors are Alphabet employees and the study was Alphabet-funded; no independent replication was found.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: g-AMIE is cloud, English, text-only, and produces an uncoded free-text SOAP note plus a patient message, with no FHIR/OPConsultRecord emission, no ABDM integration, no offline mode and no Indic languages - so it does not directly compete with MediKiosk's stated differentiation (offline-first, India data residency, NRCeS-conformant emission, per-field provenance, physician attestation) and leaves those axes open. It strengthens rather than erodes MediKiosk's case on oversight design: g-AMIE's blinded results give a citable precedent that patient-elicted history plus a physician-reviewed summary can match or exceed early-career clinician documentation quality while cutting oversight time to roughly 60% of a full consultation, which is exactly the OPD-throughput argument MediKiosk makes. Its stricter relevance is as a design/validation template - the guardrail-agent safety pattern, the cockpit UX and the rubric set - not as a deployable competitor in the Indian public-health OPD context.

business_info.license: No open-source license applies: g-AMIE is a Google research prototype. The paper's code-availability statement says the system uses Gemini (available via Google Cloud APIs) and that the multi-agent technique is described in the paper, with no code repository, weights or dataset released; onward use is stated to be gated on research-partner, regulator and provider validation. Gemini itself is a proprietary Google service.
business_info.pricing: None published for g-AMIE. Underlying Gemini 2.0 Flash inference is a paid Google Cloud/Vertex AI service under standard API pricing; the research system itself is not sold or offered as a service.
business_info.funding: Fully funded by Alphabet Inc. and/or its subsidiaries (stated competing-interests disclosure); all authors are Alphabet employees and may hold Alphabet stock. No external venture funding applies to the research artifact.
business_info.commercial_status: Non-commercial research project by Google DeepMind/Google Research. It is not a product, not a free public service and not a government programme; the broader AMIE research line is being translated into clinical studies and partnerships but g-AMIE itself remains exploratory.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Research-side: the earlier AMIE itself (Tu et al.), Polaris (Hippocratic AI), Mo (Alan Health), Therabot, K Health's intake chatbot, and non-Google conversational diagnostic agents; physician-oversight/agent-supervision literature (NP/PA co-management models). On the ambient-note and pre-visit summary commercial side: Abridge, Nuance DAX Copilot, Ambience, Sunoh.ai, EkaScribe/Eka Care, Clearstep AI Clinical Intake, and MiiHealth AI (DAINA). No competitor combines offline + ABDM/NRCeS emission + patient kiosk elicitation, which is where MediKiosk sits.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: None for g-AMIE. It is standalone research infrastructure on Gemini via Google Cloud; successor AMIE work integrates with real-world clinical workflows (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center urgent care; a nationwide randomized study with Included Health) and provides the transcript plus an automatically generated summary to the treating PCP, but there is no EHR vendor integration, no ABDM HIP/HIU/PHR gateway role and no health-locker or FHIR endpoint documented.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The AMIE research line is moving fast and is the main external pressure on MediKiosk's 'physician-mediated AI summary' positioning: a Nature paper on longitudinal disease management (June 2026), a real-world prospective feasibility study at an academic medical center (2026, 100 patients, zero safety stops, DDx contained the final diagnosis in 90% of cases), and AMIE (Video) expert-level real-time video consultations (August 2026). This signals that cloud, English-first, large-model medical AI is converging on clinician-level conversational performance, which raises the bar for evidence quality but leaves MediKiosk's differentiators (offline, India residency, ABDM/NRCeS conformance, DPDP-grade consent, CPU-only kiosk, AYUSH-aware structured history) untouched and unaddressed by Google. For a public Indian OPD procurement context, no Google AMIE product is available to buy, so it is a benchmark and design reference rather than a procurement rival.

history.release_date: 2025-07-21 (arXiv preprint 2507.15743, first public release); Google Research blog explainer published 2025-08-12.
history.key_milestones: 2024-2025: AMIE established text-based diagnostic-dialogue capability and physician-comparable performance in simulated OSCEs; AMIE extended to multi-visit and multimodal scenarios. 2025-07-21: g-AMIE introduced (asynchronous oversight paradigm, guardrail agent, SOAP-note agent, clinician cockpit) with the 60-scenario virtual OSCE. 2025-08-12: Google Research blog 'Enabling physician-centered oversight for AMIE' publicises Gemini 2.0 Flash multi-agent design and top-line results. 2026-03: real-world prospective feasibility study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (AMIE text chat up to 5 days before urgent-care appointments, 100 patients, pre-visit summary to PCP, safety supervisors, zero safety stops). 2026-06-17: Nature publication and Google blog on AMIE for longitudinal disease management across multiple visits with guideline grounding. 2026-08-11: AMIE (Video, built on Gemini 3 Flash / Gemini 3.1 Pro) demonstrates expert-level real-time video consultations; ongoing nationwide randomized virtual-care study with Included Health.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: No g-AMIE-specific update (paper revision, productisation or new g-AMIE study) was found inside the last six months; the July 2025 preprint remains the definitive g-AMIE artifact. However, the surrounding AMIE program has been highly active in this window, and that activity matters as market context: (1) a prospective real-world clinical feasibility study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center placed AMIE text chat in a live urgent-care workflow (100 patients, pre-visit history and an automatically generated summary handed to the PCP, human safety supervisors, zero safety stops, DDx contained the final chart-review diagnosis in 90% of cases and top-3 in 75%); (2) in June 2026 Google published disease-management research in Nature, extending AMIE from one-off diagnosis to longitudinal management grounded in clinical guidelines and drug formularies; (3) in August 2026 Google announced AMIE (Video), a Gemini 3-based asynchronous three-agent system (Talker/Planner/Perception) rated on par or better than PCPs in a 100-scenario, 300-consultation randomized OSCE, with top-1 diagnostic accuracy 91% vs 77% for PCPs and mean turn latency cut to ~2.6 s. Directly relevant to Module C: the BIDMC feasibility study is the clearest current evidence that an AI-generated pre-visit summary can be delivered to a physician in a real clinic, though PCPs still outperformed AMIE on practicality and cost-effectiveness of management plans.

market_positioning.target_users: Research stakeholders: Google DeepMind/Research scientists, clinical AI safety and oversight researchers, and (via the broader AMIE program) academic medical centers, health systems and clinicians evaluating physician-oversight models. Not sold to or usable by patients or hospitals as a product.
market_positioning.market_segment: Conversational diagnostic AI / clinical AI safety and physician-oversight research; adjacent to ambient clinical documentation and pre-visit intake, but positioned as a paradigm study rather than an intake product.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: In its own framing, g-AMIE is a 'framework for effective, asynchronous oversight' of conversational diagnostic AI - a 'new paradigm' in which the AI performs history taking within guardrails and 'abstains from individualized medical advice', conveying assessments to an overseeing primary care physician who 'retains accountability of the clinical decision.' Google Research states the goal as 'enabling physician-centered oversight for AMIE', exploring how AI can gather patient information and prepare a summary, proposed differential and management plan for a licensed professional to review and authorize, so that 'accountability for safety-critical medical decisions can remain with licensed physicians'.
